Model Test 4.question: ১) Diffuse soft goiter with bruit is found in which disease?
Model Test 4.exp:
Graves' disease classically presents with a diffuse, soft, vascular goiter. Increased thyroid blood flow can produce a thyroid bruit over the gland.

  • Graves' disease → diffuse soft goiter + bruit

  • Hashimoto's thyroiditis → usually firm, irregular goiter

  • Subacute thyroiditis → painful/tender thyroid

  • Multinodular goiter → irregular/nodular enlargement

Exam pearl:
“Diffuse soft goiter + bruit → Graves' disease.”

Model Test 4.question: ২) The nervous system originated from which germ layer?
Model Test 4.exp:
The nervous system develops from the ectoderm, specifically the neural plate, which forms the neural tube during neurulation.

  • Ectoderm → nervous system + epidermis

  • Endoderm → gastrointestinal and respiratory epithelium

  • Paraxial mesoderm → vertebrae, skeletal muscle, dermis

  • Lateral plate mesoderm → cardiovascular system, body wall, connective tissues

Exam pearl:
“Nervous system = Ectoderm.”

Model Test 4.question: ৩) Which one is called policeman of abdomen?
Model Test 4.exp:
The greater omentum is called the “policeman of the abdomen” because it moves toward sites of inflammation or infection and helps localize and wall off intra-abdominal infection.

  • Greater omentum → Policeman of abdomen

  • Lesser omentum → connects liver to stomach and duodenum

  • Mesentery → suspends and supplies the small intestine

  • Mesoappendix → suspends the appendix

Exam pearl:
“Policeman of abdomen = Greater omentum.”

Model Test 4.question: ৪) Which poisoning causes Hypothermia?
Model Test 4.exp:
Opioid poisoning can cause hypothermia due to depression of the central nervous system and impaired thermoregulation.

Typical opioid toxicity features:

  • CNS depression/coma

  • Respiratory depression

  • Miosis (pinpoint pupils)

  • Hypothermia

Other options:

  • Salicylate poisoning → hyperthermia is more characteristic.

  • NSAID poisoning → GI/CNS symptoms, metabolic acidosis in severe cases

  • SSRI poisoning → serotonin syndrome → hyperthermia

Exam pearl:
“Opioid poisoning → respiratory depression + miosis + hypothermia.”

Model Test 4.question: ৫) Sexual signaling caused by pheromones is secreted by......?
Model Test 4.exp:
Pheromones involved in sexual signaling are classically associated with secretions from apocrine sweat glands, particularly in areas such as the axilla and anogenital region.

  • Apocrine glands → associated with pheromonal/sexual signaling

  • Eccrine glands → thermoregulation

  • Sebaceous glands → sebum secretion

Exam pearl:
“Sexual signaling/pheromones → Apocrine sweat glands.”

Model Test 4.question: ৬) What is the content of Callot’s triangle?
Model Test 4.exp:
Calot’s (hepatobiliary) triangle contains the cystic artery, which is an important landmark during cholecystectomy.

Boundaries of Calot’s triangle:

  • Cystic duct

  • Common hepatic duct

  • Inferior surface of liver

Contents:

  • Cystic artery

  • Cystic lymph node (node of Lund)

  • Lymphatics and connective tissue

Exam pearl:
“Calot’s triangle → Cystic artery.”

Model Test 4.question: ৭) Which is endocrine cause of weight gain?
Model Test 4.exp:
Hypothyroidism is a classic endocrine cause of weight gain because reduced thyroid hormone lowers the basal metabolic rate and can cause fluid retention.

  • Hypothyroidism → weight gain

  • Thyrotoxicosis → weight loss

  • Diabetes mellitus → classically weight loss in uncontrolled Type 1 DM

  • Adrenal insufficiency (Addison’s) → weight loss

Exam pearl:
“Endocrine weight gain → Hypothyroidism.”

Model Test 4.question: ৮) What is the location of dust cell?
Model Test 4.exp:
Dust cells are alveolar macrophages found in the alveoli of the lungs. They phagocytose inhaled dust particles, microorganisms, and cellular debris.

  • Dust cell = Alveolar macrophage

  • Location → alveoli of lung

Exam pearl:
“Dust cell → Alveolar macrophage → Lung.”

Model Test 4.question: ৯) Myenteric plexus is present in which layer of GIT?
Model Test 4.exp:
The myenteric (Auerbach’s) plexus is located between the inner circular and outer longitudinal layers of the muscularis externa of the GIT.

It primarily controls:

  • Gastrointestinal motility

  • Peristalsis

  • Muscle tone

For comparison:

  • Meissner’s plexus → submucosa → secretion & blood flow

  • Auerbach’s plexus → muscularis externa → motility

Exam pearl:
“Auerbach = muscularis; Meissner = submucosa.”

Model Test 4.question: ১০) Which is not a cause of polyuria?
Model Test 4.exp:
Hypoglycemia is not a cause of polyuria.

Polyuria occurs commonly due to:

  • Hyperglycemia → osmotic diuresis

  • Cranial diabetes insipidus → ADH deficiency → water loss

  • Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus → renal resistance to ADH → water loss

Exam pearl:
“Polyuria → think hyperglycemia or diabetes insipidus; hypoglycemia does not cause polyuria.”

Model Test 4.question: ১১) Which is not a first line investigation in thyroid function test?
Model Test 4.exp:
The first-line thyroid function tests are blood tests, especially:

  • TSH → primary screening test

  • Free T4 → assesses thyroid hormone level

  • T3 → useful particularly when T3 toxicosis is suspected

Radioiodine uptake (RAIU) test is not a first-line thyroid function test. It is mainly used to determine the cause of hyperthyroidism, such as Graves’ disease versus thyroiditis.

Exam pearl:
“First-line TFT → TSH ± T4/T3; RAIU is a second-line etiological test.”

Model Test 4.question: ১২) which layer of epidermis protects against friction and water loss?
Model Test 4.exp:
The stratum corneum is the outermost layer of the epidermis and provides the main physical barrier against friction, water loss, chemicals, and pathogens.

It consists mainly of dead, keratin-filled corneocytes embedded in a lipid-rich matrix.

  • Stratum corneum → protection + prevents water loss

  • Stratum lucidum → present mainly in thick skin

  • Stratum granulosum → keratinization and formation of the epidermal barrier

  • Stratum basale → cell proliferation and regeneration

Exam pearl:
“Main barrier against friction and water loss = Stratum corneum.”

Model Test 4.question: ১৩) which one is not the content of portal triad??
Model Test 4.exp:
The portal triad consists of:

  • Portal vein

  • Hepatic artery

  • Bile duct(ule)

The hepatic vein is not part of the portal triad. It drains blood from the liver into the inferior vena cava.

Exam pearl:
“Portal triad = Portal vein + Hepatic artery + Bile duct.”

Model Test 4.question: ১৪) which is a cause of solitary nodular enlargement of thyroid gland?
Model Test 4.exp:
A colloid cyst can present as a solitary thyroid nodule (solitary nodular enlargement).

  • Colloid cyst → solitary thyroid nodule

  • Hashimoto’s thyroiditis → usually diffuse/firm thyroid enlargement

  • Graves’ disease → diffuse, vascular goiter

  • Iodine deficiency → typically diffuse or multinodular goiter

Exam pearl:
“Solitary thyroid nodule → think colloid cyst/adenoma.”

Model Test 4.question: ১৫) Which is the pace maker of heart?
Model Test 4.exp:
The SA node (SAN) is the natural pacemaker of the heart because it has the highest rate of spontaneous depolarization among the cardiac pacemaker cells.

  • SA node → 60–100 beats/min → primary pacemaker

  • AV node → 40–60 beats/min → secondary pacemaker

  • Purkinje fibers → 20–40 beats/min → tertiary pacemaker

  • Internodal pathways → conduct impulses from SA node toward AV node

Exam pearl:
“Pacemaker of heart = SA node.”

Model Test 4.question: ১৬) which is contraindicated in Pregnancy or planned pregnancy within 6 months of treatment in case of treatment of hyperthyroidism?
Model Test 4.exp:
Radioiodine (I-131) therapy is contraindicated during pregnancy because it crosses the placenta and can damage the fetal thyroid, particularly after the first trimester.

It should also be avoided when pregnancy is planned soon after treatment. The exact recommended interval can vary by guideline, but 6 months is a commonly taught exam interval.

  • Antithyroid drugs → can be used in pregnancy with appropriate drug selection

  • Subtotal thyroidectomy → may be performed when indicated, especially in the 2nd trimester

  • Radioiodine → contraindicated in pregnancy

Exam pearl:
“Hyperthyroidism + pregnancy → Radioiodine is contraindicated.”

Model Test 4.question: ১৭) dialated part of the uterus known as-
Model Test 4.exp:
The fundus is the rounded, expanded upper part of the uterus, located above the points where the uterine tubes enter.

  • Fundus → broad/rounded upper part

  • Body → main central portion

  • Isthmus → narrow constricted part

  • Cervix → lower narrow neck-like part

Exam pearl:
“Dilated/expanded upper part of uterus = Fundus.”

Model Test 4.question: ১৮) which structure enters through renal hilum?
Model Test 4.exp:
The renal hilum transmits the renal vessels, ureter, nerves, and lymphatics.

From anterior → posterior, the classic arrangement is:

Renal Vein → Renal Artery → Renal Pelvis/Ureter (V-A-P)

So, renal vein, ureter, nerves, and lymphatics all pass through the renal hilum. However, since the question asks “which structure enters” and multiple listed structures can pass through the hilum, the MCQ is ambiguous.

If the intended answer is the structure that enters the kidney rather than exits, renal artery and nerves enter, while the renal vein and ureter leave the hilum.

Exam pearl:
Renal hilum = Vein + Artery + Pelvis/Ureter + Nerves + Lymphatics.

Model Test 4.question: ১৯) The classic symptoms of primary hyperparathyroidism excludes.....?
Model Test 4.exp:
The classic mnemonic for primary hyperparathyroidism is:

“Stones, bones, abdominal groans, and psychic moans.”

  • Stones → renal calculi due to hypercalcemia

  • Bones → bone pain/osteitis fibrosa

  • Abdominal groans → constipation, abdominal pain, nausea

  • Psychic moans → depression, confusion, cognitive changes

Therefore, “moans” alone is not the complete classic feature; “psychic moans” is the actual mnemonic component.

Exam pearl:
Hyperparathyroidism → “Stones + Bones + Abdominal groans + Psychic moans.”

Model Test 4.question: ২০) what is the cause of euvolaemic hypernatremia?
Model Test 4.exp:
Euvolemic hypernatremia occurs when there is a loss of free water without significant loss of sodium, so the extracellular fluid volume remains relatively normal.

The classic cause is diabetes insipidus (DI) due to either:

  • ↓ ADH secretion → central DI

  • Renal resistance to ADH → nephrogenic DI

Other options:

  • Diuretic therapy → usually causes hypovolemia

  • Excessive sweating → water and salt loss → hypovolemia

  • SIADH → euvolemic hyponatremia, not hypernatremia

Exam pearl:
“Euvolemic hypernatremia → Diabetes insipidus.”

Model Test 4.question: ২১) which is not true about nephritic syndrome ?
Model Test 4.exp:
Nephritic syndrome is characterized mainly by glomerular inflammation, resulting in:

  • Hematuria → often with RBC casts

  • Oliguria → due to reduced GFR

  • Hypertension → due to sodium and water retention

  • Mild to moderate proteinuria

Overt/heavy proteinuria is more characteristic of nephrotic syndrome, where proteinuria is typically >3.5 g/day in adults.

Exam pearl:
Nephritic = Hematuria + Hypertension + Oliguria + mild/moderate proteinuria.
Nephrotic = Heavy proteinuria + Hypoalbuminemia + Edema.

Model Test 4.question: ২২) A respiratory bronchiole leads to.........?
Model Test 4.exp:
The respiratory bronchiole is part of the respiratory portion of the lung and continues into the alveolar ducts, which then lead to alveolar sacs and alveoli.

Pathway:

Terminal bronchiole → Respiratory bronchiole → Alveolar duct → Alveolar sac → Alveoli

Exam pearl:
“Respiratory bronchiole → Alveolar duct.”

Model Test 4.question: ২৩) which one is a feature of type-2 DM?
Model Test 4.option2: rapid death without treatment with insulin
Model Test 4.exp:
Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is strongly associated with family history, obesity, insulin resistance, and increasing age.

  • Family history → common in T2DM

  • Normal/low body weight → more typical of T1DM

  • Rapid death without insulin → characteristic of untreated T1DM due to DKA

  • Typical onset <40 years → more characteristic of T1DM (although T2DM can occur at younger ages)

Exam pearl:
“Type 2 DM → family history + obesity/insulin resistance + gradual onset.”

Model Test 4.question: ২৪) which one is the most common cause of Coushing's syndrome?
Model Test 4.exp:
The most common overall cause of Cushing's syndrome is iatrogenic, due to prolonged use of exogenous glucocorticoids such as prednisolone.

  • Iatrogenic → most common overall cause

  • Pituitary ACTH-secreting adenoma → most common endogenous cause (Cushing disease)

  • Ectopic ACTH syndrome → less common

  • Adrenal adenoma → less common

Exam pearl:
“Cushing syndrome overall → Iatrogenic; endogenous Cushing syndrome → Pituitary adenoma (Cushing disease).”

Model Test 4.question: ২৫) what is the lining eipithelium of thin limb of loop of Henle?
Model Test 4.exp:
The thin limb of the loop of Henle is lined by simple squamous epithelium, which facilitates passive movement of water and solutes.

  • Thin limb → simple squamous epithelium

  • Thick ascending limb → simple cuboidal epithelium

  • PCT → simple cuboidal with prominent brush border

Exam pearl:
“Thin limb of Loop of Henle = Simple squamous epithelium.”

Model Test 4.question: ২৬) The pralidoxime dose for an adult in OPC poisoning is......... IV over 4 mins, repeated 4–6 times daily?
Model Test 4.exp:
In organophosphorus compound (OPC) poisoning, pralidoxime (2-PAM) is used to reactivate acetylcholinesterase, particularly when given early.

For an adult, a commonly taught regimen is:

  • Pralidoxime 2 g IV, administered slowly over about 15–30 minutes in many modern protocols.

  • The older exam regimen may state 2 g IV over ~4 minutes, repeated at intervals.

Exam pearl:
“Adult OPC poisoning → Pralidoxime 2 g IV.”

Model Test 4.question: ২৭) which disease is diagnosed by water deprivation test?
Model Test 4.exp:
The water deprivation test is used to evaluate polyuria and polydipsia, particularly to diagnose diabetes insipidus (DI).

After water deprivation:

  • Normal person → urine becomes concentrated

  • Diabetes insipidus → urine remains dilute

  • Desmopressin response can then help differentiate:

    • Central DI → urine concentrates significantly

    • Nephrogenic DI → little or no response

Exam pearl:
“Water deprivation test → Diabetes insipidus.”

Model Test 4.question: ২৮) What is the type of neuron in the sensory neurons of the retina?
Model Test 4.exp:
The bipolar cells of the retina act as intermediate sensory neurons, transmitting signals from photoreceptors (rods and cones) to ganglion cells.

Retinal pathway:

Rods & cones → Bipolar cells → Ganglion cells → Optic nerve

  • Bipolar → sensory neurons/interneurons of retina

  • Ganglion cells → multipolar neurons

  • Pseudounipolar → typical of dorsal root ganglia

Exam pearl:
“Retinal sensory pathway → Photoreceptor → Bipolar → Ganglion.”

Model Test 4.question: ২৯) Vitiligo is a feature of which disease?
Model Test 4.exp:
Vitiligo is associated with Addison's disease because both can result from autoimmune disorders. In autoimmune Addison's disease, destruction of the adrenal cortex may occur along with autoimmune destruction of melanocytes, causing depigmented patches.

  • Addison's disease → hyperpigmentation + may be associated with vitiligo

  • Cushing's syndrome → cortisol excess

  • Conn's syndrome → primary hyperaldosteronism

  • Pheochromocytoma → catecholamine excess

Exam pearl:
“Addison's + vitiligo → think autoimmune polyglandular syndrome.”

Model Test 4.question: ৩০) what is the location of Chromaffin cells?
Model Test 4.exp:
Chromaffin cells are specialized neuroendocrine cells located mainly in the adrenal medulla. They secrete the catecholamines:

  • Adrenaline (epinephrine)

  • Noradrenaline (norepinephrine)

They are derived embryologically from neural crest cells and are considered modified postganglionic sympathetic neurons.

Exam pearl:
“Chromaffin cells → Adrenal medulla → Catecholamines.”

Model Test 4.question: ৩১) hyponatremia occurs when plasma sodium level is below...... mmol/L?
Model Test 4.exp:
Hyponatremia is defined as a serum/plasma sodium concentration <135 mmol/L.

  • Normal Na⁺: approximately 135–145 mmol/L

  • Hyponatremia: <135 mmol/L

  • Severe hyponatremia: often considered <125 mmol/L

Exam pearl:
“Na⁺ <135 mmol/L = Hyponatremia.”

Model Test 4.question: ৩২) what is the cause of maximum percentage of deaths in a people with DM?
Model Test 4.exp:
In people with diabetes mellitus, the major cause of death is cardiovascular disease (CVD) due to accelerated atherosclerosis and associated vascular complications.

Common cardiovascular complications include:

  • Coronary artery disease

  • Myocardial infarction

  • Stroke

  • Peripheral arterial disease

Other options:

  • DKA → important acute complication, especially in type 1 DM

  • Renal failure → major diabetic complication, but not the leading overall cause of death

  • Infections → increased risk, but less common as the primary cause of death

Exam pearl:
“Diabetes mellitus → leading cause of death = Cardiovascular disease.”

Model Test 4.question: ৩৩) which type of vessels are major determinant of systemic blood pressure?
Model Test 4.exp:
Arterioles are the major resistance vessels and therefore the principal determinant of systemic vascular resistance and systemic blood pressure.

They regulate blood pressure mainly by changing their vascular smooth muscle tone, causing vasoconstriction or vasodilation.

  • Arterioles → major determinant of systemic BP

  • Arteries → conduct blood and provide elastic recoil

  • Veins → capacitance/reservoir vessels

  • Venules → collect blood from capillaries

Exam pearl:
“Arterioles = resistance vessels = major regulator of systemic BP.”

Model Test 4.question: ৩৪) what is the location of Seminiferous tubules?
Model Test 4.option4: From rete testis to head of epididymis
Model Test 4.exp:
Seminiferous tubules are located within the testicular lobules and are the site of spermatogenesis.

Each testicular lobule contains 1–4 highly coiled seminiferous tubules.

Pathway of sperm:
Seminiferous tubules → straight tubules → rete testis → efferent ductules → epididymis

Exam pearl:
“Seminiferous tubules → Testicular lobules.”

Model Test 4.question: ৩৫) Which neuroglial cell aid production and movement of CSF?
Model Test 4.exp:
Ependymal cells line the ventricles of the brain and central canal of the spinal cord. Specialized ependymal cells in the choroid plexus help in CSF production, while their cilia aid CSF movement/circulation.

  • Ependymal cells → CSF production and movement

  • Astrocytes → support, blood-brain barrier

  • Oligodendrocytes → myelination in CNS

  • Schwann cells → myelination in PNS

Exam pearl:
“CSF production & movement → Ependymal cells.”

Model Test 4.question: ৩৬) which oral antidiabetic drug is incretin mimetics?
Model Test 4.exp:
Vildagliptin is a DPP-4 inhibitor, which increases endogenous incretin hormones (GLP-1 and GIP) by preventing their breakdown.

Strictly speaking, vildagliptin is an incretin enhancer, not an incretin mimetic. True incretin mimetics include GLP-1 receptor agonists such as exenatide and liraglutide.

Among the given options:

  • Vildagliptin → DPP-4 inhibitor → incretin effect

  • Metformin → biguanide

  • Glimepiride → sulfonylurea

  • Rosiglitazone → thiazolidinedione

Exam pearl:
“Vildagliptin → DPP-4 inhibitor → ↑ endogenous incretin effect.”

Model Test 4.question: ৩৭) ejaculation requires......... stimulation?
Model Test 4.exp:
Ejaculation is primarily mediated by the sympathetic nervous system, mainly through T11–L2 spinal segments.

The sexual response is classically summarized as:

  • Erection → Parasympathetic (S2–S4)

  • Ejaculation → Sympathetic (T11–L2)

  • Emission → Sympathetic

  • Expulsion → Somatic (pudendal nerve)

Exam pearl:
“Point and shoot: Parasympathetic = erection; Sympathetic = ejaculation.”

Model Test 4.question: ৩৮) what type of capillaries are present in choroid plexus?
Model Test 4.exp:
The choroid plexus contains fenestrated capillaries, which allow relatively free exchange of substances between blood and the surrounding tissue.

However, the blood–CSF barrier is maintained by the tight junctions between the choroid plexus epithelial (ependymal) cells, not by the capillaries themselves.

  • Choroid plexus → fenestrated capillaries

  • Blood–CSF barrier → tight junctions of choroid plexus epithelium

Exam pearl:
“Choroid plexus = Fenestrated capillaries + tight epithelial junctions.”

Model Test 4.question: ৩৯) most of the developing ovarian follicles arrest and degenerate with apoptosis in a process called .....?
Model Test 4.exp:
Follicular atresia is the process by which most developing ovarian follicles degenerate and undergo apoptosis rather than progressing to ovulation.

  • Atresia → degeneration of ovarian follicles

  • Only a small number of follicles reach full maturity and undergo ovulation.

  • It occurs throughout reproductive life and is especially prominent before puberty and after menopause.

Exam pearl:
“Ovarian follicle degeneration by apoptosis = Atresia.”

Model Test 4.question: ৪০) which is a microvascular complication of DM?
Model Test 4.exp:
Diabetic retinopathy is a classic microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus.

Microvascular complications:

  • Retinopathy

  • Nephropathy

  • Neuropathy

Macrovascular complications:

  • Myocardial infarction (MI)

  • Stroke

  • Peripheral arterial disease

DKA is an acute metabolic complication, not a microvascular complication.

Exam pearl:
“DM microvascular complications = Retinopathy + Nephropathy + Neuropathy.”

Model Test 4.question: ৪১) Which delicate neuronal layer directly contacts neural tissue?
Model Test 4.exp:
The pia mater is the innermost and most delicate meningeal layer. It closely adheres to and directly covers the surface of the brain and spinal cord.

Meninges from outer → inner:

Dura mater → Arachnoid mater → Pia mater

  • Pia mater → directly contacts neural tissue

  • Arachnoid mater → lies beneath dura and does not closely follow brain contours

  • Dura mater → tough outer layer

  • Arachnoid granulations → project into dural venous sinuses and absorb CSF

Exam pearl:
“Meningeal layer directly contacting brain/spinal cord = Pia mater.”

Model Test 4.question: ৪২) which is a post renal cause of AKI?
Model Test 4.exp:
Post-renal AKI results from obstruction to urinary outflow.

Urinary calculi (stones) can obstruct the ureter, causing increased back pressure on the kidneys and reducing GFR.

  • Urinary calculi → Post-renal AKI

  • Dehydration → Pre-renal AKI

  • Drugs → commonly intrinsic renal AKI (depending on the drug)

  • CCF → Pre-renal AKI due to reduced renal perfusion

Exam pearl:
“Post-renal AKI = urinary tract obstruction → stones, prostate enlargement, tumors.”

Model Test 4.question: ৪৩) which is site of phonation?
Model Test 4.exp:
Phonation is the production of voice by the vibration of the vocal folds, which are located in the larynx.

  • Larynx → site of phonation

  • Pharynx → resonance and passage for air/food

  • Trachea → conducts air

  • Bronchi → conduct air to the lungs

Exam pearl:
“Phonation = Larynx.”

Model Test 4.question: ৪৪) which is the feature of DKA?
Model Test 4.exp:
Acetone (fruity) breath is a classic feature of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). It occurs due to increased production of ketone bodies, particularly acetone, during severe insulin deficiency.

Other features of DKA include:

  • Kussmaul respiration — deep, rapid breathing

  • Dehydration

  • Tachycardia

  • Abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting

  • Altered consciousness in severe cases

Exam pearl:
“DKA → acetone/fruity breath + Kussmaul breathing.”

Model Test 4.question: ৪৫) what is the lining eipithelium of endometrium?
Model Test 4.exp:
The endometrium (mucosa of the uterus) is lined by simple columnar epithelium.

  • Endometrium → Simple columnar

  • Contains uterine glands that are also lined by simple columnar epithelium.

  • The epithelium undergoes cyclical changes during the menstrual cycle under hormonal influence.

Exam pearl:
“Endometrium = Simple columnar epithelium.”

Model Test 4.question: ৪৬) in which poisoning large pupil occurs?
Model Test 4.exp:
Cocaine poisoning causes mydriasis (large/dilated pupils) due to increased sympathetic activity.

  • Cocaine → Mydriasis

  • Opioids → Miosis (pinpoint pupils)

  • Clonidine → Miosis

  • Organophosphorus (OPC) poisoning → Miosis

Exam pearl:
“Large pupils (mydriasis) → Cocaine; Pinpoint pupils (miosis) → Opioids/OPC.”

Model Test 4.question: ৪৭) what is the feature of somatic neuropathy?
Model Test 4.exp:
Somatic neuropathy affects somatic sensory and motor nerves. Carpal tunnel syndrome is a median nerve entrapment neuropathy, so it is a somatic peripheral neuropathy.

The other options are features of autonomic neuropathy:

  • Gustatory sweating → autonomic neuropathy

  • Postural hypotension → autonomic neuropathy

  • Erectile dysfunction → autonomic neuropathy

Exam pearl:
“Somatic neuropathy → Carpal tunnel syndrome; Autonomic neuropathy → postural hypotension + erectile dysfunction + gustatory sweating.”

Model Test 4.question: ৪৮) In Pheochromocytoma there is hypersecretion of which hormone?
Model Test 4.exp:
Pheochromocytoma is a tumor of chromaffin cells, usually arising from the adrenal medulla, causing excessive secretion of catecholamines:

  • Adrenaline (epinephrine)

  • Noradrenaline (norepinephrine)

  • Sometimes dopamine

Classic clinical features include episodic headache, sweating, palpitations, and hypertension.

Exam pearl:
“Pheochromocytoma → Catecholamine excess.”

Model Test 4.question: ৪৯) which one is used to remove potassium from the body to treat severe hyperkalemia?
Model Test 4.exp:
Frusemide (furosemide) is a loop diuretic that increases urinary potassium excretion, thereby helping to remove potassium from the body in hyperkalemia when adequate renal function and urine output are present.

Other options:

  • Calcium gluconate → stabilizes cardiac membrane; does not lower serum K⁺

  • Salbutamol → shifts K⁺ into cells; does not remove it

  • Insulin → shifts K⁺ into cells with glucose; does not remove it

Exam pearl:
“Hyperkalemia: remove K⁺ → diuretics/dialysis; shift K⁺ → insulin + glucose/salbutamol; stabilize heart → calcium gluconate.”

Model Test 4.question: ৫০) what is the area number of vision in brain?
Model Test 4.exp:
The primary visual cortex is Brodmann area 17, located in the occipital lobe along the banks of the calcarine sulcus.

  • BA 17 → Primary visual cortex

  • BA 18 & 19 → Visual association areas

  • BA 22 → Wernicke's area (language comprehension)

  • BA 41 → Primary auditory cortex

Exam pearl:
“Vision = Brodmann area 17.”
